title: The Number System, Surds and Rounding
seo_title: Grade 10 Number System and Surds Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Understand that real numbers can be irrational or rational; establish between which two integers a given simple surd lies; round real numbers to an appropriate degree of accuracy (to a given number of decimal digits); simplify, add, subtract and multiply surds.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 10 worksheets: rational and irrational numbers, simplifying, adding and multiplying surds and rounding. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Real numbers are rational (can be written as a fraction) or irrational (like √2 and π).
  • Simplify a surd by taking out a square factor: √50 = √(25 × 2) = 5√2.
  • Add only like surds: 3√2 + 5√2 = 8√2, but √2 + √3 cannot be simplified.
  • √a × √b = √(ab).

Examples

Example

√18 + √8

3√2 + 2√2

Answer: 5√2

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding under the root√2 + √3 ≠ √5.
Not the biggest square√12 = 2√3.
Recurring is irrational0,333… = ⅓ is rational.

items.q: Between which two whole numbers is √216?
items.e: 14² = 196 and 15² = 225. 216 is between them, so √216 is between 14 and 15.

items.q: Which whole number is √140 closest to?
items.e: 140 is between 11² = 121 and 12² = 144, and closer to 144. So √140 is closest to 12.
